title: Revenue is up, so why are pricing power and margins collapsing? Operating risk at 400 K-brands in 2026
summary: A survey of 400 K-brands: 63% are losing margin to unauthorized distribution. Get the free 2026 report and see how the top 7.5% kept control of their pricing.
body_markdown:
[K-brand exports grew 172.2% over the past five years, a record run approaching the growth rate of semiconductor exports (178.7%).](https://supple.kr/news/cmrcurnmi001j1loytpz19ucj)


Yet when MarqVision and Remember Research surveyed 400 Korean brands, 8 in 10 (81%) said counterfeits and the gray market were directly hurting their revenue. Revenue is growing while profitability falls. Here’s what the data says about why.


## Record exports, shrinking profits: the brand profitability paradox


K-brands’ global growth shows in the numbers. In the first half of 2026 alone,[K-beauty exports reached $7 billion, K-food $6.6 billion and K-bio $4.5 billion](https://www.cosinkorea.com/news/article.html?no=57785) , with all three industries breaking their all-time records.


Add the Korean Wave effect, where[every $100 million increase in K-content exports raises related consumer goods exports by $202 million](https://v.daum.net/v/20260709092449747) , and brands in every industry are rushing to sell directly through global e-commerce.


Yet many brand teams are asking:


> *“Revenue has clearly grown, so why are our pricing power and margins collapsing?”*


The more global e-commerce channels expand, the easier it is for unauthorized resellers to get in. They buy up stock in bulk through Korean distribution, use AI translation to get onto local marketplaces, and dump products at 30% below the official store’s price.


K-beauty brand A, which had entered Southeast Asia, couldn’t hold out against this gray-market push. Just one year after its official launch, it had lost control of its global pricing entirely and had to pull out of the market. ( *Source: Woman Donga, July 3, 2025* )


## We asked 400 K-brands directly | MarqVision × Remember Research


To find out, **MarqVision and Remember Research** surveyed 400 large and mid-sized Korean companies that have gone global or are preparing to, about how they run their brands. Respondents ranged from assistant managers up to department heads and other decision-makers, across fashion, luxury and beauty; consumer goods, home and leisure; and B2C healthcare and pharma.


The results were clearer than expected.


### 81%: lost up to 20% of revenue to counterfeits and gray-market sales


81% of respondents had experienced direct revenue loss from counterfeits and gray-market distribution, with losses reaching up to 20%.[The global market for counterfeit K-brand products is worth $9.7 billion a year (about 11.1 trillion won), and 35.9% of it is K-beauty. China is the shipping country for 97.7%.](https://v.daum.net/v/8AYmXrEoCr)


The bigger problem: these losses often aren’t even measured. According to MarqVision × Remember Research, 74.5% of companies that had lost revenue measured it only irregularly or not at all. 3% of executives (decision-makers) said quantitative measurement was impossible, compared with 58% of practitioners, revealing a paradox in which executives know less about the reality than their teams.


### 95%: don’t know how their brand appears in AI search


[About 20% of global e-commerce spending during the 2025 holiday season (about $262 billion) was influenced by AI and agents](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/2025-holiday-shopping-data/) , and[traffic to US retail sites from generative AI jumped 693% year over year](https://dito.fashion/DigitalInnovation/?bmode=view&idx=171077883) . As agentic commerce takes off, a new threat is spreading fast: AI search engines that learn from manipulated data recommend counterfeit and gray-market products as genuine.


82% of respondents had already experienced AI-driven threats, yet only 14% regularly monitor their brand in AI search and recommendation services. The report covers how many companies can trace the cause when AI recommends a counterfeit as genuine, and how wide the monitoring gaps are by industry.


## What the top 7.5% that kept their pricing power do differently


Some brands kept growing through the same crisis. Only 7.5% of companies connect internal and external data in real time for integrated analysis, and they have something in common.


They manage threats as a business KPI, not as a cost.


The companies that protected their margins quantified revenue loss every month and reported it to leadership. They used data to spot pricing issues before they happened, and their sales and IP teams shared live status on the same dashboard so they could act at once. The report shows exactly what they managed and how.
